objections.claim: The all-tags ruleset does not close the Releases API surface granted by `contents:write`. GitHub immutable releases still permit editing the published release title and notes/body, yet the candidate stores the sole Eye-signed RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE block in that mutable body and unsuspends the controller/publisher Apps after post-publish verification. Either App can then PATCH the body without changing the protected tag or immutable assets; the integrity sweep detects the loss only after the public authority record has changed. Separately, a public release can be created against an already-existing tag without creating or updating that ref, so the all-tags ruleset cannot prevent publication unless every existing tag is proven already bound to an accepted immutable release. Move the canonical acceptance into an immutable signed/attested allowlisted asset, treat the body only as a non-authoritative pointer, enforce an exact existing-tag/release invariant, and add post-publish body-mutation and existing-tag publication regressions. Until then blocker 6's fail-closed release contract remains unresolved at `fc0fa05`.
